blocks.prompt: 9 Find the equation of the image of the curve with equation \(y = x^2\) under the transformation with associated matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\).
blocks.explanation:
A whole curve is transformed: every point \((x, y)\) moves to \((x', y')\).
We must find the equation the new points satisfy.
Plan: \(x', y'\) from the matrix; reverse with \(M^{-1}\); substitute in \(y = x^2\); simplify; check with one point.
steps:
Given: the curve \(y = x^2\) and the matrix \(M = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\).
To find: the equation of the image curve.
Method: A point \((x, y)\) goes to \((x', y')\) with \(\begin{bmatrix}x' \\ y'\end{bmatrix} = M\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\) (column vector, as in Example 16). Express \(x, y\) in terms of \(x', y'\) with \(M^{-1}\) and substitute in \(y = x^2\).

New coordinates in terms of old
\[\begin{bmatrix}x' \\ y'\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\]
\[x' = x + 2y\]
\[y' = 3x + 4y\]
Why: Row 1 of \(M\) times the column gives \(x'\); row 2 gives \(y'\).

Inverse of \(M\)
\[|M| = (1)(4) - (2)(3) = -2\]
\[M^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{-2}\begin{bmatrix}4 & -2 \\ -3 & 1\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}-2 & 1 \\ \frac{3}{2} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{bmatrix}\]
Why: For a \(2 \times 2\) matrix: swap the diagonal entries, change the signs of the other two, divide by the determinant.

Old coordinates in terms of new
\[\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} = M^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}x' \\ y'\end{bmatrix}\]
\[x = -2x' + y'\]
\[y = \dfrac{3x' - y'}{2}\]
Check: \(x + 2y = -2x' + y' + 3x' - y' = x'\) and \(3x + 4y = -6x' + 3y' + 6x' - 2y' = y'\).
Why: Multiplying \(\begin{bmatrix}x' \\ y'\end{bmatrix} = M\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}\) on the left by \(M^{-1}\) undoes \(M\).

Substitute into \(y = x^2\)
\[\dfrac{3x' - y'}{2} = (y' - 2x')^2\]
\[3x' - y' = 2(y'^2 - 4x'y' + 4x'^2)\]
\[3x' - y' = 8x'^2 - 8x'y' + 2y'^2\]
Why: Every old point obeys \(y = x^2\); replacing \(x\) and \(y\) by their expressions gives the rule the new points obey. Multiply by 2 and expand \((p - q)^2 = p^2 - 2pq + q^2\).

Bring to one side and drop the primes
\[8x^2 - 8xy + 2y^2 - 3x + y = 0\]
Why: The primes only marked the new points; the image curve is written in the usual \(x, y\).

Check with a point
\((1, 1)\) lies on \(y = x^2\); its image is \((1 + 2, 3 + 4) = (3, 7)\).
\[8(9) - 8(21) + 2(49) - 9 + 7\]
\[= 72 - 168 + 98 - 9 + 7 = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The image of a point of the old curve must lie on the new curve.
